messages:
anna: Quick sync — we need a concrete plan for image attestation + runtime enforcement before the next Dedicated customer onboarding. Thinking SBOM + signature + admission checks. who's owning the signing key RBAC?
ben: I can own the signing workflow. prefer cosign with KMS-backed key (GCP/AWS) so keys aren't stored in CI. need a clear approval flow for who can sign prod images. :thumbsup:
chris: Runtime enforcement: we should block unsigned images at admission and also have a fail-open metric for staging. OPA gate can check cosign signature + SBOM hash.
devon: We have an existing OPA bundle for pod policies. extending it is fine, but curious about performance — adding verification on pull may add latency. maybe verify at image push + store attestation in registry and only check attestation ref at admission.
lisa: Good point. We can store attestations in the registry (cosign attestations) and check a lightweight pointer during admission. Also add a mutating webhook to inject runtime seccomp/profile hints.
anna: @ben what RBAC do you need? list of roles? also we need audit entries for all signing actions to tie to ticket IDs for compliance.
ben: Proposal: a SigningAdmins group (prod-only) who can sign releases; CI-service account can create unsigned candidate images but cannot sign. Signing requests must reference an internal ticket (JIRA ID). We log: signer, key-id, image-digest, ticket. Logs should be forwarded to our central audit log (stackdriver->long-term storage).
chris: For incident response, if we detect an unsigned/altered image in prod, run automated isolate: cordon node, scale down affected service, and snapshot registry. Need runbook entries. Security-oncall should be paged.
security-bot: Incident note: last month staging had a mismatched SBOM for one image (INC-2024-154). Root cause was CI caching an old layer. Recommend adding SBOM generation step in pipeline and validating digest before signing.
anna: Action items: 1) ben draft RBAC/approval doc, 2) devon + chris prototype OPA attestation check (lightweight), 3) lisa add SBOM step to pipeline and cosign integration, 4) create runbook for unsigned-image detection.
ben: Drafting RBAC doc now — will include sample IAM policies and audit-sink config. Example cosign sign command for CI -> will include in doc:
```
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign --key kms://gcpprojects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/cosign-key \
  --annotations "ticket=INC-2025-001,build=123" \n  gcr.io/redwood-inference/base:2025-03-22
```
chris: For the OPA check pseudo-code I sketched: check registry.attestation[image.digest].signed_by in SigningAdmins OR env=staging. If not, deny. We'll keep a short-circuit for canary lanes.
devon: I ran a quick perf test: verifying cosign signature from registry metadata adds ~50ms median to admission call if attestation is cached in memcached; ~400ms if fetching remote each time. So caching is required.
lisa: On vuln triage: if an image component has CVEs, we should reject signing until fixed or mitigated. Add an allowlist for emergency hotpatch images with documented justification and TTL.
anna: Let's meet tomorrow 10am to review the RBAC doc + runbook. Please post your PRs to #eng-security for visibility. Also tag @security-oncall in the runbook for paging rules. :calendar: :lock:
security-bot: Deploy job succeeded: test-signing-pipeline (build 456) — cosign attestation created and logged.
ben: Uploaded RBAC doc draft: https://internal.docs/redwood/sec/signing-rbac (comments welcome).
chris: I'll open OPA PR w/ unit tests for attestation lookup and caching. linking when ready.
anna: Thanks all — this should close the main gaps before customer onboarding. If anyone spots a blocker DM me.
